title: Pager cache reset and data-version publication

scope.rationale: pager_reset publishes one wrapping data-version change, restarts attached backup observations, and discards the complete page cache as one invariant-preserving operation.
excluded_responsibilities: Deciding when external database or WAL changes require reset

external_source_responsibilities: Page cache clear releases all unreferenced cached pages
Backup owner observes data-version changes when retaining a serialized source image
dependencies.caller_closure: The complete straight-line source body is assigned; hot recovery, WAL read/change, and external file-version invalidation paths consume resetCache. Other cache.clear sites represent transaction-local invalidation rather than source pager_reset.

inputs: Mutable Pager with no live cache references at reset boundaries
outputs: Wrapping u32 data_version increment and empty Pager cache
contracts.ownership: Cache.clear consumes cache-owned page allocations. Pager and VFS ownership are retained.
contracts.state_and_results: Increment data_version exactly once using source-width wrapping arithmetic, then discard all cached pages. Connection backup logic treats a changed version as a restart boundary.
contracts.locks_callbacks_io: No direct locks or I/O; callers own synchronization. Backup restart is represented by the shared version boundary rather than a callback list inside Pager.
contracts.failure_and_continuation: Infallible. Cache clear is non-allocating and leaves a reusable empty cache.

representation_differences: Production Pager stores the source-width u32 data_version directly; the older internal model used a u64 with truncating accessor.
The connection backup owner polls Pager data version instead of Pager storing the source intrusive pBackup list; this preserves restart detection without cross-module pointer ownership.

oracle.protocol: Open and release one 512-byte cached page, seed data_version to max-u32, call resetCache, and require wrapped zero plus zero cache pages. Existing hot-journal, WAL recovery, checkpoint, rollback, and external-version tests exercise production callers.
internal_observations: cache page count before and after reset
oracle.normalization: Compare exact u32 modular value and exact cache page count.

assurance.io_crash_concurrency: No I/O; caller lock and reference-count preconditions external.
assurance.malformed_input: Typed Pager and cache invariants constrain input.
assurance.continuation: The empty cache remains reusable after reset.
assurance.performance: Linear in cached page count due to complete release.

integration.native_call_path: recoverHotJournal and beginRead WAL/external-change handling call resetCache; Backup polls Pager.dataVersion and restarts a retained partial image after changes; transaction-local checkpoint and rollback invalidation remain separate cache operations.
integration.bounded_owner_retired: Direct cache.clear calls at source reset-equivalent recovery and external-change boundaries are retired.

independent_review.notes: Requires public data-version/backup restart integration trace, pinned-C reset trace, assurance closure, and independent review.

known_blockers: Add pinned-C reset and backup restart trace.
